stage_findings: The 4096-byte UDP payload begins as one 4124-byte IPv4 datagram. IA emits one 4180-byte ESP packet with DF clear. R creates four ESP fragments at offsets 0,1256,2512,3768. IB reassembles one outer packet before ESP processing; HB receives the exact public payload digest.

With a 1200-byte Red MTU, HA emits four plaintext UDP fragments. IA reassembles them before encryption and emits one outer ESP packet. R fragments that packet again. IA and IB each increment ReasmOKs once; the receiver obtains the exact 4096-byte payload. The provisional test plan statement about separately encrypted plaintext fragments was corrected to the observed reassemble-before-encrypt behavior.

The overlapping plaintext fragments cover [0,1600) and [800,2400), with the same ID and a valid complete UDP union. IA increments IpReasmFails and IpExtReasmOverlaps once. No ESP packet leaves IA and no UDP payload arrives. A later valid full-size payload succeeds.

Two valid IPv6 fragments with immediate NH44 pass the original priority -300 raw check after priority -400 netfilter reassembly; the public 1800-byte UDP payload arrives. The repaired priority -450 nftables check drops both fragments before reassembly. Its counter increments by two packets and 1904 bytes. Valid 256-byte IPv6 UDP passes before and after.
source_binding: Linux v6.8 include/uapi/linux/netfilter_ipv6.h defines before-defrag -450, defrag -400 and raw -300. nf_defrag_ipv6_hooks.c registers defragmentation at -400. The observed nftables JSON binds the active -450 gate and literal ip6 nexthdr expression.

nf_defrag_ipv4.c registers IPv4 fragment gathering at the corresponding defrag priority. inet_fragment.c detects overlaps, and ip_fragment.c handles the failed queue. Actual kernel counters and packet records provide the local stage observation.

The actual kernel is an Ubuntu distribution build. uname, /proc/version, installed kernel config, module paths/vermagic/srcversion, XFRM state/policy, conntrack availability and namespace identities remain in raw commands. Upstream v6.8 source is a reviewed implementation-family reference; no byte identity with the distribution build is invented.
scope: One owned manually provisioned Linux IPv4 ESP path, not IKE or native FRR/OVS. Captures retain complete requested IP/ESP header metadata and omit encrypted bodies. Final application reports payload size and SHA-256.
The IPv6 fragment test is an active local gate with valid below-MTU controls. Dynamic ICMPv6 PMTU and external L2TP encapsulator fragmentation remain separate tasks.
Only newly created owned namespaces and their MTUs/filters are changed. They are removed after collection. Existing deployments remain preserved.
